title: Searching and counts
summary: Find text with / ? n N * #, and multiply any motion with a count.

steps.title: Search
body: | `n` | next match in the same direction |
| `N` | next match in the opposite direction |
| `*` | search forward for the whole word under the cursor |

Searches **wrap around** the end of the file (vim says `search hit BOTTOM, continuing at TOP`). The pattern is a regular expression: `/^server` finds lines starting with `server`, `/port\s*=` allows spaces. `:noh` clears the highlighting.
> **Practise:** open **Labs → Vim & nano trainer** and run this lesson's challenges until the keys come without thinking.

steps.prompt: Match the keys to the search.
pairs: next occurrence of the word under the cursor

steps.prompt: You searched with `?TODO`. You press `N`. Which way does the cursor move?
options: Down (forward): N reverses the search's direction
It repeats the last f motion
steps.explain: `n` follows the direction of the last search (`?` is backward), `N` goes the other way.

steps.title: Counts
body: Put a number in front of almost any motion to repeat it:
10G     line 10 (for G the count is a line number)
Counts work with operators too: `3dd` deletes three lines, `d2w` deletes two words. With relative line numbers turned on (module 5) the numbers you need are printed down the side.

steps.prompt: The cursor is on line 10 of a 100-line file. You press `5j`, then `2k`, then `G`, then `3k`. Which line are you on?
Order the keystrokes to jump to the third match of `listen` below the cursor.
steps.explain: The search itself lands on the first match; `2n` moves two more.

steps.title: Search with wrap-around
prompt: Write `(int Row, int Col) Search(List<string> lines, int row, int col, string pattern, bool forward)` modelling `/pattern` (forward) and `?pattern` (backward) as a plain substring search (case-sensitive):
- forward: the first match that starts **after** `(row, col)`, scanning to the end of the file, then wrapping to the top and continuing up to and including `(row, col)` itself.
- backward: the first match that starts **before** `(row, col)` going up, wrapping from the top to the bottom.
- no match anywhere: return `(row, col)` unchanged.
A line may contain several matches; consider each start position.
starter: (int Row, int Col) Search(List<string> lines, int row, int col, string pattern, bool forward)
solution: (int Row, int Col) Search(List<string> lines, int row, int col, string pattern, bool forward)
var all = new List<(int Row, int Col)>();
bool After((int Row, int Col) p) => p.Row > row || (p.Row == row && p.Col > col);
bool Before((int Row, int Col) p) => p.Row < row || (p.Row == row && p.Col < col);
foreach (var p in all) if (After(p)) return p;
for (int i = all.Count - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (Before(all[i])) return all[i];
hints: Collect every match position in file order first.
Forward: the first one after the cursor, else the very first. Backward: the last one before, else the very last.
template: var dojoFile = new List<string> { "server {", "  listen 80;", "  listen 443;", "}", "# listen here" };
Dojo.Eq("forward to the next line", (1, 2), Search(dojoFile, 0, 0, "listen", true));
Dojo.Eq("forward skips the match under the cursor", (2, 2), Search(dojoFile, 1, 2, "listen", true));
Dojo.Eq("forward wraps to the top", (1, 2), Search(dojoFile, 4, 2, "listen", true));
Dojo.Eq("backward wraps to the bottom", (4, 2), Search(dojoFile, 0, 0, "listen", false));
Dojo.Eq("several matches on a line", (0, 2), Search(new List<string> { "a a a" }, 0, 0, "a", true));
Dojo.Eq("only match is under the cursor", (0, 0), Search(new List<string> { "xy" }, 0, 0, "x", true));
